intro: Grad students get the worst version of the WashU housing search: you are admitted in spring after the best places are taken, you are often signing from another city or country, and every guide is written for undergrads picking a party block. This page is for you.

The short geography: med students live in the Central West End next to the medical campus. Law and business students cluster in Clayton, DeMun, and the quieter streets of Skinker-DeBaliviere. PhD students spread everywhere the stipend stretches, which usually means University City and Skinker-DeBaliviere. Listings on Proximity show real walk and transit context so you can judge an address you have never seen.
directAnswer: WashU graduate students mostly live in the Central West End (medical campus), Clayton and DeMun (law and business, quieter and more polished), and University City and Skinker-DeBaliviere (best value near the Danforth campus). Most grad students sign between March and June after admission, later than the undergraduate cycle, and remote signing with video tours is normal.

faqs.q: Where should I live for the med campus versus the main campus?
faqs.a: The campuses are separate places connected by Metrolink and Forest Park. For the medical campus, live in the Central West End and walk. For the Danforth campus, live in Skinker-DeBaliviere, University City, or near the Loop. Living between them works but means commuting to both. Decide where your daily life happens first, then pick the neighborhood.

faqs.q: How do I sign a lease from another city or country?
faqs.a: It is normal here. Ask for a live video tour, not just photos; a legitimate landlord expects this. Verify the listing is real by checking reviews and the landlord's identity before sending any money. Proximity has toured apartments for students who could not visit, which is exactly the situation many incoming international students are in.

faqs.q: What if I have no US credit history or guarantor?
faqs.a: Common for international students and fresh admits. Many landlords accept alternatives: a larger deposit, prepaid months, proof of stipend or funding, or a university-based guarantor service. Ask each landlord what they accept before assuming you are stuck. Some of the larger buildings have formal international-student processes; small landlords decide case by case.

faqs.q: When should incoming grad students start looking?
faqs.a: The moment you accept your offer. The grad wave runs roughly March through June, and WashU affiliated companies like Quadrangle and Parallel open signing in spring, which times well for admits. By July the market thins to leftovers and subleases, though people do find places all summer.

Scarce, and grad students compete with each other for them. If you find a furnished place that fits your budget, move on it. Otherwise budget for basic furniture or look at subleases, which often come furnished because the current tenant is leaving their setup.
